b: "It must be a very weird situation, when just a few years back you were in a war fighting for your life and now you are in an office building selling ketchup and commodities." -/u/johnshall
So this is all inspired by a Veteran's Day thread in /r/madmen
Particularly this comment by /u/SouthpawMox, which seems far-fetched:

"Really random piece of that time period that the writers captured well was that in the sixties, you could assume that basically every man of a certain generation had served, and that a good number of them (often ones you would not suspect) had probably killed people in an up close and personal way."
I'm suspicious of this claim. Huge numbers of men were mobilized by the US for World War 2, but only a fraction saw combat, and then another fraction still would've taken the lives of another human.
